checksum: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC over the frame payload or snapshot body

vectors.meaning: RLOGWAL1 header and no committed frames

invariants: A WAL frame is length_le_u32 || crc32_le_u32 || payload.
A batch is operation_count_le_u32 followed by ordered tagged operations; tag 0 is put and tag 1 is delete.
A snapshot is RLOGSNP1 || payload_length_le_u64 || crc32_le_u32(payload) || payload; payload starts with entry_count_le_u32 and sorted key/value entries.
Incomplete final WAL frame is truncated on reopen; a complete bad-checksum frame is corruption.
Only a whole decoded frame mutates the recovered map, preserving batch atomicity.
Snapshot encoding and decoding enforce the same max_snapshot_entries bound; over-limit encoding fails before a temporary snapshot file is created.
A returned write error is absent after reopen; a successful write is present after reopen.
Rollback failure poisons the handle, retains its exclusive lock, and rejects subsequent operations.
Metadata and compaction failures occur after commit and are reported only through maintenance_error.
The default write policy flushes but defers synchronization until an explicit durable boundary.
